commands.command: is right, and i need to retract a specific claim i made above. i wrote that the docs "name the paths that still cancel and keep history: provider throw, missing model, missing credentials." a configured provider that throws is **not** one of them. ```js } catch (err) { // caller cancellation and real transport timeouts remain terminal. if (signal?.aborted || (!isaborterror(err) && istimeouterror(err))) throw err; log.warn(`compaction provider "${compactionprovider.id}" failed, falling back to llm: ...`); } ``` the exception is caught and execution continues into built-in llm summarization. enumerating the terminal sites at the reviewed head confirms it from the other direction - four cancel sites, and a provider throw is in none of them: | site | reason | |---|---| | `:1239` | could not resolve a summarization model | | `:1248` | `authresult.reason` (credentials) | | `:1411` | finalized summary failed quality checks and corrective generation failed | | `:1528` | could not summarize the session | so all three pages named a path that cannot happen, and `docs/reference/session-management-compaction.md` contradicted itself: line 254 said a provider throw cancels while line 255 already documented the fallback. one refinement on the suggested wording. "say that a failed built-in generation after fallback is terminal instead" is right but incomplete - a caller-initiated abort and a real transport timeout **are** re-thrown, per the guard above. all three pages now say: provider throw or empty result falls back to built-in summarization; a failed built-in generation, an unresolvable model, and missing credentials cancel and keep history; aborts and transport timeouts are re-thrown. ## both nits from @hansen1018 **test naming.** renamed to `retains the generated split-turn section when a final audit failure degrades to the fallback`, so the title matches the in-test comment. **a dedicated test for `degradetofallbacksummary`.** i did not extract it, and i want to be explicit about the tradeoff rather than quietly skip it. it is a closure over seven bindings (`log`, `finalizesummarytext`, `buildstructuredfallbacksummary`, `effectiveprevioussummary`, `splitturnsectionlocal`, `preservedturnssectionlocal`, `producerlosses`). extracting it means parameter plumbing on a production file whose diff size is already flagged as a merge risk in this review. instead i went looking for what was actually unguarded, and found a real gap: `degrades when audit-required tail sections cannot fit the artifact cap` sets `issplitturn: false` and `recentturnspreserve: 0`, so it never checked composition. **only the audit path was protected.** the new test drives the *retention* path with a split turn and asserts the same artifact composition, which is the "single fallback owner" property both reviews care about. ### evidence `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts` ``` before tests 139 passed (139) after tests 140 passed (140) exit 0 ``` mutation-checked, restored byte-identical (`sha256 45f7fc5ebe00ba75`): | mutation | result | |---|---| | drop `generatedsplitturnsection` from the degraded path | **2 failed** / 138 passed, exit 1 | | restored | 140 passed, exit 0 | that mutation failed **one** test before this commit and fails **two** after it, on both terminal entry points - which is the coverage claim, stated as a measurement rather than an assertion. run on node 24.18.0, matching the version this repo's ci pins. ##
